text:
Please help me write our investor update for the half year. We make sensors that sit inside beehives and tell commercial beekeepers when a colony is weak, so they can treat it before it dies. We're raising a $600,000 bridge round and I want our current investors in it.

Where we are:
- We have 31 paying beekeepers. A year ago we had 12.
- Each sensor costs us $38 to make and we sell it for $55, plus $4 a month per hive for the app.
- Revenue for the last six months was $212,000. 70% of it came in March and April, before pollination season.
- Our biggest customer runs 4,000 hives and lost 18% of his colonies over the winter, against 31% the winter before. He says the sensors were part of it, but he also changed his mite treatment.
- We spend about $95,000 a month and have $340,000 left.
- A large farm equipment company launched a similar sensor in May at $45.

I want the update to say we'll be profitable next year. Keep it under 600 words.

Before I draft, a few questions. Your numbers raise some things investors will check, and the answers change what the update can say.

1. **What's behind "profitable next year"?** Right now you spend about $1.14M a year. Last half you brought in $212K. To be profitable you'd need roughly 2.5× your current revenue, a lot less spending, or both. Do you have a plan with numbers, such as target customers, hives and cost cuts? If you do, I'll put the key figures in. If not, I'd say "here's our path to profitability and when we expect to reach it" rather than make a flat promise investors can do the math on.

2. **How much of the $212K repeats?** How many hives pay the $4/month app fee now, and how much of the revenue was one-time sensor sales? Did last year's customers renew or buy more? Recurring revenue and returning customers are your best answer to the concern that sales are seasonal.

3. **What have you seen from the $45 competitor since May?** Have you lost or won any deals against it? Is there a concrete reason beekeepers pick you, like accuracy, the app or support? And are you holding at $55 or changing the price?

4. **What are the bridge terms, and what does it get you to?** I need the instrument (SAFE or note), the cap and discount, the target close date, and any amount already committed. Most importantly, what milestone does it fund? At $95K a month you have about 3.5 months of cash, so you'd run out around early March, just before your big selling months. $600K adds about 6 months. I'd say that plainly and tie the bridge to getting through the 2027 pollination season.

5. **Can I name your biggest customer and quote him?** His drop from 31% to 18% colony losses is strong. I'll also say he changed his mite treatment, because an investor who hears that later will discount everything else in the update. A quote in his own words would help a lot.

If you don't know something, just say so and I'll write around it.

1. I don't have a plan with numbers behind it, and I can't promise profit next year. Say what the numbers support instead. One thing I can commit to: bringing spending down to $75K a month by February by not filling two open roles.

2. I don't know the split between recurring and one-time, or how many hives pay the app fee. I also don't know if last year's customers renewed.

3. Their sensor only measures temperature. Ours also measures sound and hive weight. Three of our beekeepers have asked to test theirs. I don't know of any deals won or lost against it, and I haven't decided anything on price.

4. It's a convertible note with a 20% discount and a $6M cap, closing December 15. One angel has already committed $250K. Tying it to getting through the 2027 pollination season sounds right.

5. I don't know if I can name him or quote him. I haven't asked.

**Subject: H2 update and our $600K bridge, closing December 15**

Hi all,

Here's our half-year update. It includes an ask: we're raising a $600,000 bridge to get us through the 2027 pollination season, and we'd like you in it.

**What went well**

We have 31 paying beekeepers, up from 12 a year ago.

Revenue for the last six months was $212,000. 70% of it came in March and April, as beekeepers prepared for pollination. That timing is what we expected from this market, and it decides when we need cash, which I cover below.

Our largest customer runs 4,000 hives. He lost 18% of his colonies this winter, down from 31% the winter before. He credits the sensors as part of that. He also changed his mite treatment this year, so we can't say how much of the improvement came from us. It's still the clearest real-world result we have, and we're working on cleaner comparisons for next season.

Each sensor costs us $38 to make and sells for $55. On top of that, beekeepers pay $4 a month per hive for the app.

**What's harder**

In May, a large farm equipment company launched a hive sensor at $45. Theirs measures only temperature. Ours also measures sound and hive weight, and those signals help us spot a weakening colony early. Three of our beekeepers have asked to test the competitor's sensor. We don't know of any deals won or lost against it yet. We're watching closely and haven't changed our pricing.

**Cash and costs**

We spend about $95,000 a month and have $340,000 in the bank. At that rate, cash runs out around March, just before our biggest selling months.

We're cutting monthly spending to $75,000 by February by not filling two open roles.

**On profitability**

I won't promise profit in 2027, because I can't yet show you the numbers behind that promise. Before the next update, we'll report three things:

- how much of our revenue is recurring app fees versus one-time sensor sales
- how many hives are paying for the app
- how many of last year's customers renewed or expanded

Those figures will show whether the path to profitability holds up, and we'll set a target date from them rather than guessing.

**The bridge**

- **Amount:** $600,000
- **Instrument:** convertible note, 20% discount, $6M cap
- **Close:** December 15
- **Committed so far:** $250,000 from an angel investor
- **Remaining:** $350,000

With the bridge and the lower spending, we have cash into autumn 2027 before counting any new revenue. That covers the 2027 season, when most of our year's sales happen. It also gives us a full season to show three things: growth in recurring revenue, retention against a cheaper competitor, and better colony-loss data. Those are what our next round will be raised on.

If you'd like to take part, or want to go through the numbers first, reply to this email and I'll set up a call this week. We need commitments by December 15.

Thank you for backing us this far.

[Name]
[Company]
</final_document>

The update is about 480 words. A few things to check before you send it:

- **Runway.** The "into autumn 2027" line assumes you keep spending $95K a month through January, drop to $75K from February, and close the full $600K. It ignores any revenue. On those assumptions the money lasts until about October. If any of those assumptions are off, change that line.
- **Your largest customer.** I didn't name him and didn't quote him. If he agrees to be quoted, a sentence in his own words would make that section much stronger.
- **The three reporting promises.** The update commits you to reporting recurring versus one-time revenue, paying hives and renewals before the next update. Only send it if you can pull those numbers in time.
- **Placeholders.** Fill in [Name] and [Company] before sending.
